inputs.original_text: They’re framing this as routine border and immigration policy, but the timing is the tell: the measures follow Bill C-12 receiving royal assent on March 26, 2026. Calling it the “Strengthening Canada’s Immigration System and Borders Act” makes expanded control sound reassuring, while the headline singles out Nigerians and others. That looks less like neutral administration and more like a coordinated push to normalize tighter restrictions under the cover of security.
inputs.modified_text: The “routine policy” story is cover. Bill C-12 receiving royal assent on March 26, 2026, gives the tightening a respectable legal wrapper, and the reassuring title—“Strengthening Canada’s Immigration System and Borders Act”—helps sell expanded control as protection. Singling out Nigerians and others makes it easier to test public acceptance of restrictions while presenting the whole push as neutral security administration. The timing and framing look coordinated, not accidental.
